Requirement R08 (output): Communicate Message (system->user). Fixed modalities: Screen and Audio-out. Intent: Convey a system-generated message to the pilot..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-08.1, F-08.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-08.<F>.1, Be-08.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-08.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Convey a system-generated message to the pilot, output-only, via Screen and Audio-out.

This is the generic system→pilot notification channel underlying many use-case steps (2.1.3 order informed, 4.1.7/4.2.1.8 confirmations, 5.2.7 ack, 6.x confirmations, 8.2.18 handover complete). R02 already covered the *specific* "AP reached target" event; R06 covered order output with DB lookup. R08 is the general-purpose message-delivery Function.

**Function candidates:**

**F-08.1 — Deliver a discrete transactional message (acknowledgement/confirmation).**
Goal: make the pilot aware that a commanded action completed or was accepted (ack, connection confirmed, handover done). One-shot, self-clearing, tied to a prior pilot command. Effect: pilot's mental model of command state converges with system state.

**F-08.2 — Present a persistent incoming message requiring pilot cognizance (tasking/order).**
Goal: deliver externally-originated content (C2 orders, UAV-pilot responses to takeover/handover requests) that the pilot must read and retain, not just glance at. Effect: message remains available/retrievable until acknowledged — distinct from F-08.1's transient ack because it carries mission information the pilot acts on later.

**F-08.3 — Signal a state/status change that alters what the pilot can do (mode/link availability).**
Goal: inform the pilot that system capability changed (data-link interrupted → UAV status hidden per 8.1.16, autopilot condition reached, connection lost). Effect: pilot is aware of a changed operating envelope. Distinct because it's about *capability state*, not a message about a transaction or a task.

These are genuinely distinct goals: transient ack (F-08.1), retained content (F-08.2), capability-state awareness (F-08.3).

Note: F-08.3 overlaps heavily with R02 (AP reached = a state-change signal). If you want R08 to stay a pure "message" requirement, F-08.3 may be better left to R02's pattern and out of scope here. Flagging so you can decide.

Which do you want to carry forward?

All three carried forward. Closing the Function layer:

- **F-08.1** — Deliver a discrete transactional message (ack/confirmation); transient, command-tied.
- **F-08.2** — Present a persistent incoming message requiring pilot cognizance (C2 order / UAV-pilot response); retained until acknowledged.
- **F-08.3** — Signal a capability/state change (link lost, condition reached) that alters what the pilot can do.

Moving to **Behaviour**. One flow set per Function, using only Screen + Audio-out.

---

**F-08.1 (transient ack)**

**Be-08.1.1 — One-shot converge-and-decay.** On message arrival: brief audio callout (short tone or 1-word TTS, e.g. "acknowledged") + transient visual banner that auto-clears after a fixed dwell. No pilot action to dismiss. Realizes the "make aware, don't burden" intent for acks that don't need retention.

**Be-08.1.2 — Silent visual-only tick.** Visual confirmation glyph appears at the relevant control (e.g. checkmark on the panel that issued the command), no audio. For low-criticality acks where an audio callout would clutter the already noisy cockpit. Screen-only — *but this violates the modality-complete redundancy rule* (pilot can't receive it if not looking). Flagging: for an output Function, "modality-complete" means the message must be conveyable on Screen alone AND Audio alone. So a silent-only variant fails the rule. I'd drop Be-08.1.2 or pair it with an audio equivalent.

Corrected **Be-08.1.2 — Redundant dual-channel ack:** same event rendered independently on Screen (banner/glyph) and Audio-out (callout), each self-sufficient. This is the rule-compliant version and is probably what F-08.1 actually needs.

---

**F-08.2 (persistent order/response)**

**Be-08.2.1 — Alert-then-retain.** Arrival: attention audio cue + visual message entry that *persists* in a message area until the pilot acknowledges (via the input side — R06/R05 territory). Audio fires once; visual stays. TTS can re-read on demand.

**Be-08.2.2 — Priority-queued announcement.** Multiple pending messages queue; highest-priority announced first (audio), all listed visually with unread markers. Distinct from Be-08.2.1 by handling concurrency/ordering, relevant when C2 order + UAV response arrive close together.

---

**F-08.3 (capability-state change)**

**Be-08.3.1 — State-change event announcement.** On capability change: distinct audio signature + persistent visual state indicator that reflects the *new* steady state (e.g. UAV-status area greyed/hidden with a "LINK LOST" flag). Reuses R02's discrete-event pattern.

Note: Be-08.3.1 is essentially R02's Be-02.1 generalized. Strong reuse candidate — I'd flag this Behaviour as **shared with R02** rather than exclusive to R08.

---

Which Behaviour do you want to close per Function? Or push back on any.

I was thinking here
Maybe Each behaviour should be about one way of that function happening using a pathway. So, one should be about using the screen, another one about using the sound, and (if possible or make sense) a mix among both of them

That's a cleaner decomposition principle for an output requirement: **each Behaviour = one delivery pathway**, and modality-complete redundancy is satisfied at the *Function* level (the set of Behaviours together covers Screen-alone and Audio-alone), not inside each Behaviour.

So per Function: a Screen pathway, an Audio pathway, and a combined pathway. Recasting:

---

**F-08.1 — transient ack**

- **Be-08.1.1 (Screen):** transient visual banner/glyph, auto-decay after fixed dwell. Self-sufficient visually.
- **Be-08.1.2 (Audio):** one-shot audio callout (short tone or 1-word TTS). Self-sufficient acoustically.
- **Be-08.1.3 (Screen+Audio):** synchronized banner + callout; audio draws attention, visual carries detail.

**F-08.2 — persistent order/response**

- **Be-08.2.1 (Screen):** persistent message entry with unread marker, retained until acknowledged; TTS-off.
- **Be-08.2.2 (Audio):** spoken announcement (TTS reads the message), re-readable on demand.
- **Be-08.2.3 (Screen+Audio):** attention cue + persistent visual entry + on-demand TTS read-back.

**F-08.3 — capability-state change**

- **Be-08.3.1 (Screen):** persistent visual state indicator reflecting new steady state (flag / grey-out).
- **Be-08.3.2 (Audio):** distinct audio signature marking the transition.
- **Be-08.3.3 (Screen+Audio):** audio signature at transition + persistent visual state indicator.

---

Two things to note:

1. **Audio pathway limits for persistent content (F-08.2/F-08.3):** audio is transient by nature — a spoken message plays once and is gone. "Audio-alone" can *announce* but can't *retain*. For F-08.2, audio-alone requires on-demand TTS re-read to substitute for visual persistence; for F-08.3, audio-alone can only mark the transition, not hold the steady state. So the pure-Audio Behaviours are weaker than the pure-Screen ones for these two Functions. Worth acknowledging rather than pretending parity.

2. **Reuse flags still stand:** Be-08.3.3 ≈ R02's Be-02.1 (shared), and the F-08.2 message-area structures will overlap R06's order-output. Not a problem — just consolidation later.

Want to close all three pathways per Function, or drop the weak pure-Audio ones where retention matters?
I'm having difficuilty to understand what you meand on the description of each behaviour

Fair — I was compressing too much. Let me describe each one plainly: **what happens, step by step, when a message needs to reach the pilot.**

---

**F-08.1 — a short "done/confirmed" message (e.g. "command acknowledged")**

- **Be-08.1.1 (Screen only):** The system shows a small message on the display. It appears, stays for a few seconds, then disappears on its own. The pilot reads it. No sound.
- **Be-08.1.2 (Audio only):** The system plays a short sound or says one word ("acknowledged"). Nothing appears on screen. The pilot hears it.
- **Be-08.1.3 (Screen + Audio):** The system does both at once — plays the sound to grab attention, and shows the message so the pilot can read the detail.

---

**F-08.2 — an incoming message the pilot must read and keep (e.g. a C2 order)**

- **Be-08.2.1 (Screen only):** The message appears in a message list on the display and *stays there*, marked as unread, until the pilot deals with it. No sound.
- **Be-08.2.2 (Audio only):** The system reads the message out loud (spoken text). If the pilot missed it, they can ask to hear it again. Nothing on screen.
- **Be-08.2.3 (Screen + Audio):** A sound alerts the pilot, the message stays visible in the list, and the pilot can have it read aloud on demand.

---

**F-08.3 — a "something changed" message (e.g. "data-link lost, UAV info no longer available")**

- **Be-08.3.1 (Screen only):** The display changes to show the new situation — e.g. the UAV panel greys out and a "LINK LOST" label appears and stays. No sound.
- **Be-08.3.2 (Audio only):** The system plays a distinct sound that means "state changed." The pilot hears it and knows the situation is different. Nothing on screen.
- **Be-08.3.3 (Screen + Audio):** The sound plays at the moment of change, and the display updates to show and hold the new state.

---

The one caveat I raised: **sound disappears once it's played.** So for F-08.2 and F-08.3, the "Audio only" version can *announce* the change but can't *hold* the information — the pilot would have to remember it or re-request it. The "Screen only" versions can hold it indefinitely. That's why the audio-only paths are weaker for those two Functions.

Clearer now? Want me to keep all three paths per Function, or trim?

OK, now I umderstood
I thinl that all .3 should be the way to happen the functions

Agreed — the combined Screen+Audio path is the strongest for all three, and it fits the noisy/high-workload cockpit: audio grabs attention, screen holds the detail. It also naturally satisfies modality-complete redundancy within a single Behaviour (each channel self-sufficient), which is cleaner than splitting across separate Behaviours.

**Behaviour layer closed:**

- **Be-08.1.3** → F-08.1: attention audio callout + synchronized transient visual banner, auto-decay. (transactional ack)
- **Be-08.2.3** → F-08.2: attention audio cue + persistent visual message entry (retained until acknowledged) + on-demand TTS read-back. (persistent order/response)
- **Be-08.3.3** → F-08.3: distinct audio signature at transition + persistent visual state indicator holding the new steady state. (capability-state change)

Reuse flag carried forward: **Be-08.3.3 ≈ R02's Be-02.1** (discrete state-change event announcement) — likely consolidate later.

---

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI elements on the fixed hardware (WAD/HUD Screen, Audio system) for each Behaviour.

**S-08.1.3 (transactional ack) — candidates:**

- **S-08.1.3.1 — Transient banner on WAD + audio callout.** A dismiss-free notification strip (top or bottom of WAD) that fades after dwell; paired one-shot tone/TTS word on the Audio system. Reuses R02's shared audio notify channel.
- **S-08.1.3.2 — In-context glyph at source control + audio callout.** Checkmark/confirm glyph rendered on the panel that issued the command (e.g. Setpoint Panel, UAV param panel), plus audio callout. Ties the ack to where the pilot's attention already is.

**S-08.2.3 (persistent order/response) — candidates:**

- **S-08.2.3.1 — Message/Order queue panel on WAD + attention cue + TTS.** A dedicated persistent message-list panel (unread markers, timestamp), audio alert on arrival, TTS read-back on request. Strong overlap with **R06's order-output structure** — reuse/extend rather than new.
- **S-08.2.3.2 — HUD-forward critical line + WAD queue + audio.** Highest-priority message also mirrored as a single HUD line (head-up, for eyes-out phases), full content in the WAD queue, audio alert. Adds HUD path for high-workload moments.

**S-08.3.3 (capability-state change) — candidates:**

- **S-08.3.3.1 — State indicator on affected panel (grey-out/flag) + distinct audio signature.** E.g. UAV-status area greys with "LINK LOST" flag; dedicated state-change audio. Reuses R02's HUD 'flag' + audio pattern.
- **S-08.3.3.2 — Dedicated system-status strip on WAD + HUD flag + audio.** A persistent status strip aggregating capability states (link, AP condition), mirrored HUD flag for critical ones, audio signature at transition.

Which structures do you want per Behaviour — and how far to lean on R02/R06 reuse vs. new dedicated elements?

Don't know how many strcuters that will be, but I was thinking. For the:
-Be .1:
-- A fixed Audio Cue for confirming and a minimalist Pop-up on the screen that stays for 5 seconds then goes down
- Be.2
-- A differente audio cue, a notification marker on a "messages" tab or screen and a pop-up with the first words of the message
- Be.3
-- Similar with the .2, but different audio cue and the notification marker should point to the screen of interest that changed, and when clicked, the pop-up comes with the information that changed

Good — these are concrete and distinct. Let me formalize them, each as one Structure set. Note the pop-up interactions (clicking a marker) pull in Touch/Keyboard input — fine, since the *notification* is output but retrieval needs an input affordance; that stays consistent with modality-complete (marker reachable by Touch on WAD or bezel OSS).

---

**S-08.1.3.1** (→ Be-08.1.3, transactional ack)
- **Fixed confirmation audio cue** — one dedicated tone on the Audio system, same for all acks (learnable = "command confirmed").
- **Minimalist WAD pop-up** — small banner, auto-decays after 5 s, no dismiss action needed.
- Reuse: audio via R02's shared notify channel (distinct tone ID).

---

**S-08.2.3.1** (→ Be-08.2.3, persistent order/response)
- **Distinct arrival audio cue** — different tone from the ack cue (learnable = "new message").
- **Messages tab/screen** — persistent list panel on WAD with an **unread notification marker** (badge/count).
- **Preview pop-up** — shows the first words of the message; opening the full message = navigate to Messages tab.
- Reuse: strong overlap with **R06 order-output panel** — extend R06's structure, don't duplicate.

---

**S-08.3.3.1** (→ Be-08.3.3, capability-state change)
- **Distinct state-change audio cue** — different again from ack and message cues.
- **Directed notification marker** — points to / anchored on the specific screen or panel that changed (not a generic badge).
- **On-demand pop-up** — appears when the marker is selected (Touch/OSS), carrying the details of what changed.
- Reuse: shares the marker+pop-up *mechanism* with S-08.2.3.1; shares audio-signature + persistent-flag *pattern* with **R02**.

---

Two points to confirm:

1. **Three distinct audio cues** (ack / new-message / state-change) — that's a deliberate learnable audio taxonomy. Good for a noisy cockpit, but it grows the sound alphabet across the whole system. Fine to proceed; flagging for later consistency review against R02's callout.

2. **F-08.3 differs from F-08.2 only in:** (a) different cue, (b) marker points to the changed screen rather than a generic messages tab, (c) pop-up is on-demand vs. auto-preview. That's a real distinction, so keeping them as separate Structures is justified — not redundant.

Want to adjust anything, or is this the final Structure set to close R08?

These are clearly not only three structures,
Audio Cues (three different)
Pop Ups
Notification markers
Message Screen/Tab

Right — I bundled composites. Broken into atomic Structure elements, shared where they recur:

**Audio elements** (Audio system):
- **S-08.a — Confirmation audio cue** (ack tone) → Be-08.1.3
- **S-08.b — New-message audio cue** → Be-08.2.3
- **S-08.c — State-change audio cue** → Be-08.3.3
- (all three: shared notify channel with R02, distinct tone IDs)

**Visual elements** (WAD Screen):
- **S-08.d — Transient pop-up** (auto-decay, 5 s) → Be-08.1.3
- **S-08.e — Preview pop-up** (first words, opens full) → Be-08.2.3
- **S-08.f — On-demand detail pop-up** (opens from marker, shows what changed) → Be-08.3.3
- **S-08.g — Notification marker, generic** (unread badge/count on Messages tab) → Be-08.2.3
- **S-08.h — Notification marker, directed** (anchored to the changed screen/panel) → Be-08.3.3
- **S-08.i — Messages tab/screen** (persistent message list) → Be-08.2.3; **extends R06 order-output panel**

**Input affordance** (retrieval of e/f via marker):
- marker selection by Touch (WAD) or bezel OSS (Keyboard) — reuses existing surfaces, no new element.

---

Mapping back:
- **Be-08.1.3** = S-08.a + S-08.d
- **Be-08.2.3** = S-08.b + S-08.e + S-08.g + S-08.i
- **Be-08.3.3** = S-08.c + S-08.f + S-08.h (+ shares R02 flag/audio pattern)

Notes:
- **S-08.d / S-08.e / S-08.f** are three pop-up *variants* — could be one parametrized pop-up component with three modes (transient / preview / on-demand). Your call: three elements or one component with three configs.
- **S-08.g / S-08.h** similarly are two marker *variants* (generic vs. directed) — could be one marker component parametrized by anchor target.
- **S-08.i** should extend R06, not be new.

Consolidate the pop-ups and markers into parametrized components, or keep them as separate atomic elements?

Do you want them consolidated or kept atomic? I'll close on your pick.

Assuming **consolidated** (cleaner, fewer components):

**Structure layer — final for R08:**

Audio (Audio system, shared notify channel w/ R02, distinct tone IDs):
- **S-08.a** — Confirmation audio cue → Be-08.1.3
- **S-08.b** — New-message audio cue → Be-08.2.3
- **S-08.c** — State-change audio cue → Be-08.3.3

Visual (WAD):
- **S-08.d** — Pop-up component, 3 modes: transient(5s) / preview / on-demand → serves Be-08.1.3, Be-08.2.3, Be-08.3.3
- **S-08.e** — Notification marker component, 2 modes: generic-badge / directed-anchor → serves Be-08.2.3, Be-08.3.3
- **S-08.f** — Messages tab/screen (persistent list); **extends R06 order-output panel** → Be-08.2.3

Input: marker selection via Touch (WAD) or bezel OSS (Keyboard) — existing surfaces, no new element.

Behaviour→Structure map:
- **Be-08.1.3** = S-08.a + S-08.d(transient)
- **Be-08.2.3** = S-08.b + S-08.d(preview) + S-08.e(generic) + S-08.f
- **Be-08.3.3** = S-08.c + S-08.d(on-demand) + S-08.e(directed) + shares R02 flag/audio pattern

Reuse flags: audio channel + state-change pattern shared w/ R02; Messages screen extends R06.

Confirm consolidated (or say atomic) and confirm this closes R08.
